title: Aurones in medicinal chemistry: synthetic strategies, biological activities, structure–activity relationships and challenges
content: Aurones are 2-benzylidenebenzofuran-3(2H)-ones whose compact conjugated framework supports broad substitution, semisynthesis and pharmacophore hybridization. This review adds a chemistry-to-evidence framework that was not provided by earlier activity-centred surveys: it defines the boundary between aurones and related scaffolds, links each synthetic diversification strategy to matched-series SAR, separates experimental target evidence from computational hypotheses, and compares translational maturity across therapeutic areas. A reproducible literature audit through July 2026 integrates classical chalcone cyclization, benzofuranone–aldehyde condensation, late-stage O-functionalization, CuAAC, glycosylation, aminoalkylation, and natural-product derivatization. Anticancer studies dominate, with the strongest progression observed for tubulin-directed semisynthetic aurones supported by cellular, mechanistic and organism-level experiments. Neurochemical, metabolic, cardiovascular, anti-inflammatory, musculoskeletal and anti-infective studies identify additional leads, but their SAR remains series- and assay-specific. The principal barriers are inconsistent structural and geometrical assignment, limited selectivity controls, sparse quantitative physicochemical and pharmacokinetic data, uncertain target engagement, incomplete tissue-exposure measurements, and little chronic safety evidence. No aurone-based approved medicine or interventional clinical study was identified. Progress therefore depends on chemically verified structures, matched-series SAR, orthogonal target validation and exposure-guided lead selection rather than further unprioritized analogue expansion.
